text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - British stocks ended on a firm note, buoyed by healthy gains on Wall Street after U.S. producer price and retail sales data soothed worries about U.S. inflation and interest rates. The FTSE 100 index jumped 33.4 points to 4,028.1, for a rise of 3.3 points for the week.

FRANKFURT- German stocks edged higher in a session hampered by uncertainty before the release of U.S. inflation data. The 30-share DAX index rose 5.28 points to 2,686.03 and was up 2.75 from last Friday. In after-hours trading the DAX index stood at 2,692.69.

PARIS - French shares also rose after the U.S. economic data, but volume was sluggish as many investors had stayed on the sidelines. The blue-chip CAC-40 index added 11.49 points to 2,147.12, but was down 5.57 points for the week.
ZURICH - Swiss shares edged higher, with the All-share Swiss Performance Index up 5.11 points to 2,435.64, up 3.73 points from last Friday.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks rose after drifting in a narrow range. The 225-share Nikkei average rose 97.33 points to close at 20,968.16, for a loss of 179.87 for the week.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended lower following its strong run up earlier in the week. The Hang Seng Index slipped 24.07 points to close at 12,218.40, for a gain of 312.89 from last Friday.

SYDNEY - The Australian market came close to a record after major issues were buoyed by stronger metal prices. The key All Ordinaries index ended 13.3 points higher at 2,336.8, up 25.1 from a week ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks closed higher despite weakness in gold shares. The all-share index rose 23 points to 7,054.5, for a rise of 33.9 from last week; the industrial index jumped 31.7 points to 8,270.4, up 48 from a week ago, and the gold index lost 11.8 points to 1,728.2, for a loss of 5.6 points on the week.
